rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God encompassed every creature and counted them; he may have enumerated them before existence in the unseen and counted them after existence.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون الإحصاء قبل الوجود في عالم الغيب والعد بعد الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No creature exists, is born, or undergoes an event before its appointed time, already counted for it.
rows.anchor: فلم يوجد ولم يولد , ولم يعد أو يصب أحد منهم إلا في حينه الذي عده له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection each comes alone and humbled, leaving wealth and children behind; no one can protect himself from extinction, so none can be God's child or partner.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا موجود غيره يقدر على حراسة نفسه من الفناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will soon give believers who act righteously great love in people's hearts as a reward for their obedience.
rows.anchor: في قلوب العباد , دالا على ما لهم عندهم من الود

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Believers receive this affection without cultivating ordinary causes of love such as kinship, charity, or favors; it is a special grace God originates.
rows.anchor: من غير تودد منهم ولا تعرض للأسباب التي تكسب بها الناس مودات القلوب من قرابة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-wudd means freedom from the will to cause harm; the author infers that God puts no enmity toward believers in righteous servants' hearts.
rows.anchor: وسيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى في سورة الروم ما يزيد ذلك وضوحا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Hurayra, God tells Gabriel and heaven to love a beloved servant, then acceptance is placed for him on earth; hatred likewise spreads for one God hates. The author says the report is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others.
rows.anchor: روى الشيخان وغيرهما عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made this unmatched Qur'an easy in clear, eloquent Arabic so the Prophet can give glad tidings to the God-fearing and warn the stubborn disputants.
rows.anchor: هذا العربي المبين , العذب الرصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing guard against what angers God, neither suppressing truth nor legitimizing falsehood, and promptly repent when they slip.
rows.anchor: يجعلون بينهم وبين ما يسخط الله وقاية , فلا يبطلون حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lidd describes someone who persists in error and hostility, refuses evidence, and tries to turn truth into falsehood out of contempt and arrogance.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يتمادى في غيه ولا يرجع لدليل , ويركب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports the Prophet defining pride as rejecting truth and despising people, distinguishing it from simply liking fine clothes and shoes; cited from Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persistent arrogance makes a person liable to die in disbelief, the gravest falsehood, and be barred from Paradise.
rows.anchor: فكان جديرا بأن يركبه الله أبطل الباطل : الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to endure mockery and other hostile speech; prayer and remembrance lift the soul toward spiritual excellence and help sustain patience.
rows.anchor: لك من الاستهزاء وغيره . ولما كان الصبر شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ with praise means worshipping God alone through prayer and remembrance, declaring him free of imperfection while affirming every perfection.
rows.anchor: حامدا له بإثبات كل كمال , وذلك بأن تصلي له خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before sunrise means dawn prayer; before sunset can mean both afternoon and noon prayers, while night hours indicate sunset and night prayers.
rows.anchor: أي بصلاة المغرب والعشاء , إيذانا بعظمة صلاة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night worship is especially excellent because hearts are settled and people are quiet and alone with God, though its greater difficulty makes it more meritorious.
rows.anchor: لأن العبادة إذ ذاك أشق وأدخل في التكليف فكانت افضل عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the command for dawn and afternoon prayers highlights their special merit; the wording also encompasses voluntary prayers throughout day and night.
rows.anchor: وكرر الأمر بصلاتي الصبح والعصر إعلاما بمزيد فضلهما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jarir ibn ʿAbd Allah reports that the Prophet compared seeing God to seeing the full moon and urged guarding the prayers before sunrise and sunset; he then recited this verse. The author says it is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
rows.anchor: ما في الصحيحين عن جرير ابن عبد الله البجلي رضي الله عنه قال : كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers reading the prayer times as dawn and afternoon before sunrise and sunset, sunset and night during some night hours, and dawn, noon, and afternoon across the day's four endpoints.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بما قبل الطلوع الصبح , وما قبل الغروب العصر فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this preferred reading, the first and last endpoints are dawn and afternoon prayers and the middle endpoints preparation for prayer and prayer itself; the prepositions mark night portions but are omitted for the active daytime.
rows.anchor: أما الأول والآخر فبالصبح والعصر , وأما الآخران فبالتهيؤ للصلاة ثم الصلاة نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording laʿalla keeps the worshipper hopeful rather than secure: God may please the Prophet with the triumph of his religion and fulfillment of all he hopes for in both lives.
rows.anchor: افعل هذا لتكون على رجاء من أن يرضاك ربك فيرضيك في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not gaze beyond an initial glance at the worldly luxuries given to disbelieving groups; those goods are a trial and do not benefit them in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لا تطول نظرهما بعد النظرة الأولى المعفو عنها قاصدا للاستحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's good, sufficient provision is better than disbelievers' adornments because it does not lead to excess and its reward endures; calling it God's provision is honorific and signals its lawful character.
rows.anchor: الكفاف الطيب المقرون بالتوفيق { خير } من زهرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to command his household to pray, as his forefather Ishmael did, so he leads them to every good; teaching others purifies sincerity.
rows.anchor: كما كان أبوك إسماعيل عليه السلام , ليقودهم إلى كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Anbiyāʾ argues that the Hour is real and near, even through death, and that judgment will encompass both the great and the insignificant.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الاستدلال على تحقق الساعة وقربها ولو بالموت ، ووقوع الحساب فيها على الجليل والحقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator has no partner able to impede the Hour and never breaks his word; the prophets' stories collectively establish this, though no single story plainly proves every point by itself.
rows.anchor: والدال على ذلك أوضح دلالة مجموع قصص جماعة ممن ذكر فيها من الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them people rather than using a pronoun evokes the instability and vacillation of those whose worship rests on a precarious edge.
rows.anchor: عبر بالناس الذي مدلولة الاضطراب والتردد دون أن يضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping on an edge is like standing at a cliff or the flank of an army: one stays only while expecting booty and flees at the first imagined danger.
rows.anchor: فهو مزلزل كزلزلة من يكون على حرف شفير أو جبل أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine wording for a trial suggests even a small bodily or financial affliction can expose this person's hidden instability.
rows.anchor: يختبر بها ويظهر خبأة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning back on one's face means a complete, settled return to former disbelief or doubt, possible only after extreme helplessness; steadfast believers instead give thanks in ease and praise God and persevere in hardship.
rows.anchor: رجع إلى الوجه الذي كان عليه من الكفر أو الشك رجوعا متمكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wavering person loses the afterlife through sin and gains no recovery of missed worldly goods; sin may itself constrict provision and remove its blessing.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب أن ذلك لا يرد ما فاته منها ويكون سبب التقتير عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report states that a person may be deprived of provision because of a sin; the segment does not identify its transmitter.
rows.anchor: إن الرجل ليحرم الرزق بالذنب يصيبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's account of a man who judged Islam good if his wife bore a son and his horses produced foals, but judged it bad otherwise.
rows.anchor: في التفسير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في هذه الآية قال : كان الرجل يقدم المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unstable worshipper then invokes besides God what can neither harm nor benefit, truly relying on something other than God and abandoning the exclusive plea for divine help.
rows.anchor: أي يعبد حقيقة أومجازا مع التجدد والاستمرار بالاعتماد على غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should seek God's protection from satanic insinuations that prod him into sins and away from good, and from the destructive presence of devils even without direct whispering.
rows.anchor: أي أن يصلوا إلي بوساوسهم التي هي كالنخس بالمهماز في الإقحام في السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest danger from devils comes at death, when the veil lifts and the person's fate becomes certain, so the passage warns believers to strive and pray for protection then.
rows.anchor: فإنه وقت كشف الغطاء , عما كتب من القضاء , وآن اللقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death the person addresses the angels of punishment and asks to return to the world, the abode of knowledge; the plural may address God and the angels, express honorific speech to a great one, or intensify the request.
rows.anchor: ويجوزأن يكون الجمع لله تعالى وللملائكة , أو للتعظيم على عادة في مخاطبات الأكابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person hopes to return only to believe and do the good he left undone, rather than to rejoin family or gather wealth and satisfy desires.
rows.anchor: ما تمنى أن يرجع إلى أهله وعشيرته ولا ليجمع الدنيا ويقضي الشهوات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi reports Qatada's view that the dying person's sole wish is to return to obey God, not to family, kin, wealth, or pleasure.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : قال قتادة : ما تمنى أن يرجع إلى أهله

rows.speaker: العلاء بن زياد
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reports al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Ziyad urging anyone who imagines death has arrived and asks God for respite to act now in obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير : كان العلاء بن زياد يقول : اينزلن أحدكم نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā decisively denies any return: the request is merely a word the person utters, known from his past deceit and lacking genuine resolve.
rows.anchor: فهو لا يجاب إليها , عطف عليه قوله , جامعا معه كل من ماثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barzakh is an unremovable barrier surrounding the dead between worldly life and resurrection.
rows.anchor: اي حاجز بين ما هو فيه وبين الدنيا والقيامة مستمر لا يقدر أحد على رفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is either the second blast of resurrection or the third blast for fainting; people then rise from graves or from their fainting.
rows.anchor: وهي نفخة النشور , أو الثالثة للصعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship will no longer be invoked for boasting or mutual aid amid terror and distraction; only righteous deeds matter, and no one can help another without God's permission.
rows.anchor: لما دهمهم من الأمر وشغلهم من البأس ولحقهم من الدهش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of questioning here concerns mutual support, while questioning elsewhere concerns blame and quarrels at different long stages of the Day, so the reports do not conflict.
rows.anchor: ولا يناقض نفي التساؤل هنا إثباته في غيره لأنه في غير تناصر بل في التلاوم والتعاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Successful people are weighed by accepted deeds; each deed may have its own appropriate scale, and the plural underscores God's power and the scope of weighing.
rows.anchor: أي بالأعمال المقبولة , ولعل الجمع لأن لكل عمل ميزانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural demonstrative may signal the many saved people or the universal weighing of every individual after the prior singular expressed the multiplicity of deeds.
rows.anchor: ولعله جمع للبشارة بكثرة الناجي بعد أن أفرد الدلالة على كثرة الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with light scales neglected faith-based deeds and lose themselves by following appetites in the abode of action; they remain forever in a Hell whose fire never dies out.
rows.anchor: باتباعها شهواتها في دار الأعمال وشغلها بأهوائها عن مراتب الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire scorches faces with intense heat; the damned are disfigured, their lips drawn back over their teeth in grim anguish.
rows.anchor: أي متقلصو الشفاه عن الأسنان مع عبوسة الوحوه وتجعدها وتقطبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewarded the believers for patience in worship despite the unbelievers' abuse, whereas their opponents' enjoyment of humiliating believers distracted them from worship.
rows.anchor: اي على عبادتي , ولم يشغلهم عنها تألمهم بأذاكم كما كما شغلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers alone are the saved victors, obtaining good after coming near destruction; the wording makes their exclusive victory clear and firmly established.
rows.anchor: اي الناجون الظافرون بالخير بعد الإشراف على الهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly triumph through mockery and dominance is negligible beside lasting punishment and reward; even the most pampered person forgets every worldly pleasure after one immersion in Hell.
rows.anchor: وكان أنعم أهل الدنيا إذا غمس في النار غمسة ثم سئل عن نعيمة قال : ما رايت نعيما قط

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the following inna with a kasra as a fresh sentence, rather than connecting it syntactically to the preceding clause.
rows.anchor: وكسر الهمزة حمزة والكسائي على الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks how many years the unbelievers spent in the worldly life they considered victory; the wording recalls constricted years and exposes their delusion about worldly success.
rows.anchor: { كم لبثتم في الأرض } على تلك الحال التي كنتم تعدونها فوزا { عدد سنين * } أنتم فيها ظافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading of the majority, God directly asks the question; Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read qul, making an appointed angel the speaker as God turns away from and punishes them.
rows.anchor: وبين سبحانه بقراءة ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي أن القول بواسطة بعض عباده الذين أقامهم لتعذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are asked about worldly years in which they thought themselves victorious and dominant over their enemies.
rows.anchor: ظنا أ , مدة لبثهم في النار تكون بمقدار مكثهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer that they stayed only a day or part of a day, minimizing worldly time beside the punishment and mistakenly supposing Hell's duration will match their earthly stay.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أيضا قصد الترقيق عليهم بالإشارة إلى أن ما هم فيه من العذاب شاغل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to the counters resembles worldly liars who ask someone else to authenticate their story; alternatively, they plead that torment has so occupied them they cannot recall or calculate the past.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أيضا قصد الترقيق عليهم بالإشارة إلى أن ما هم فيه من العذاب شاغل لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even accepting their estimate, it cannot help them because punishment follows their settled resolve to persist in defiance; God's answer truthfully calls their worldly stay very little, virtually nothing.
rows.anchor: أي هو من القلة بحيث بحيث لا يسمى بل هو عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they had truly known, they would have preferred lasting reward to transient life and abandoned the frivolity no rational person would choose.
rows.anchor: ولأقبلتم على ما ينفعكم , وتركتم الخلاعة التي لا يرضاها عاقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should thank God for the joy of their enemies' destruction, inheriting their lands, being honored and blessed with long lives, and continuing happiness in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: على الشكر على ما منحهم من السرور بإهلاك أعدائهم وإيراثهم أرضهم وديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thinking there is no resurrection led the unbelievers to delight, arrogance, and mockery of God's people, as though the just King created them purposelessly rather than to reveal justice and grace.
rows.anchor: لا لحكمة إظهار العدل والفضل , حتى اشغلتم بظلم أنفسكم وغيركم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan defines ʿabath as play devoid of benefit.
rows.anchor: والعبث : اللب الخالي عن فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may continue the earlier rebuke about taking the believers as an object of mockery, or imply that God would neglect them and fail to vindicate the wronged against their oppressors.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معطوفا على مقدر نحو : أحسبتم أنا نهملكم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Yaʿla, and al-Baghawi report from Ibn Masʿud that he recited this verse through the surah's end over a possessed man, who recovered; the Prophet said a certain believer's recitation over a mountain would move it. The chain contains Ibn Lahiʿa.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه رقى رجلا مصابا بهذه الآية إلى آخر السورة في أذنيه فبرأ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that if a man of certainty recited these verses over a mountain, it would move; the report's chain contains Ibn Lahiʿa.
rows.anchor: لو أن رجلا موقنا قرأ بها على جبل لزال

none: A bare Surah al-Nur heading only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns the heavens and earth, which are subordinated to his rule; all creatures return to him after death. The passage connects to the call to inspect the dominion in 7:185.
rows.anchor: ولله } أي الذي لا ملك سواه { ملك السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says izjāʾ is used for gently driving a heavy thing; sḥāb is a generic noun whose singular is saḥāba, and the phrase means driving one cloud toward another.
rows.anchor: إن الإزجاء يستعمل في سوق الثقل برفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates clouds from nothing, sometimes low and sometimes high, initially thin and scattered, then joins their parts and piles them into a massive mass.
rows.anchor: أي بين أجزائه بعد أن كانت قطعا في جهات مختلفة

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz explains al-wadq as rain, while another view takes it as the abundance of rain.
rows.anchor: قال القزاز : وقيل : هو احتفال المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain emerges through openings formed in the piled cloud as its parts press and condense against one another.
rows.anchor: فتوقه التي حدثت بالتراكم وانعصار بعضه من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains in the sky are clouds amassed until they resemble mountains; hail is frozen water, and God sends or withholds rain and hail by choice as mercy or punishment.
rows.anchor: وهي السحاب الذي صار بعد تراكمه كالجبال ؛ وبعض فقال : { من برد } هو ماء منعقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning nearly blinds with its brilliant flashes; its strength signals dense clouds and heavy rain and warns of possible lightning strikes.
rows.anchor: لشدة لمعه وتلألئه , فتكون قوة البرق دليلا على تكاثف السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alternates night and day, light and darkness, increase and decrease, rain and clear skies, producing heat, cold, growth, and dryness; these changes show power, comprehensive knowledge, and oneness to reflective observers.
rows.anchor: من الحر والبرد والنمو والينوع واليبس ما يبهر العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, whose sign is the moon, and day, whose sign is the sun, succeed one another with opposite qualities and replace one another in many functions, allowing what is missed in one to be made up in the other.
rows.anchor: جعلهما مختلفين في النور والظلام , والحر والبرد

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir says the Arabs use khalaf and khilfa for alternating opposites, such as light and darkness or heat and cold.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : والعرب تقول : خلف والخلفة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi in al-Lawamiʿ explains khilfa as things taking turns, each succeeding its companion, or as people who differ.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : يقال : الأمر بينهم خلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's doubled reading yadhdhakkara points to reflection through reason: change on this scale requires a powerful, choosing changer and can bring even a disbeliever to faith.
rows.anchor: بما دل عليه الإدغام في قراءة الجماهة بفتح الذال والكاف مشددتين

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza's light reading yadhkura means remembrance; the signs of divine power and knowledge are so clear that a slight attention suffices without extended reflection.
rows.anchor: وقراءة حمزة بالتخفيف من الذكر تشير إلى أن ما يدلان عليه من تمام القدرة وشمول العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternating cycles invite believers to give profound thanks: each night or day arrives before the previous one's benefits are lost, while perpetual light or darkness would produce fatigue and disrupt timed duties.
rows.anchor: أي شكرا بليغا عظيما لنعم الله لتحمله إرادته تلك على الشكر إن كان مؤمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts servants of the Merciful with servants of Satan: raising ʿibād al-Raḥmān as a new subject honors them and shows they embody mercy; he also offers a syntactic link to the preceding address as another possibility.
rows.anchor: ولعله أحسن : أنه سبحانه لما وصف الكفار في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their gentle, humble walking suits people made from earth and returning to it; they avoid harming or boasting over anyone and do not follow satanic passions.
rows.anchor: { هونا } أي ذوي هون , أي لين ورفق وسكينة ووقار وإخبات وتواضع , لا يؤذون أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural reading riyaḥ, used by most reciters rather than Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi, highlights the varied winds God can use to raise clouds.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة الجمهور بالجمع خلافا لابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي تنبيه على عظيم الصنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first makes the wind raise clouds that did not exist, then attributes spreading and dividing the clouds to himself to show that no natural force acts independently.
rows.anchor: نزع الإسناد إليها في البسط والتقطيع فإنه لم يجعل فيه قوة شيء من ذلك ليعلم أن الكل فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clouds' varied distances and forms show that God alone freely chooses how to spread them, without nature or another cause controlling him.
rows.anchor: تارة كمسيرة ساعة أو يوم , وكثيرا كمسيرة أيام على أوضاع مختلفة تدلك قطعا على أنه فعله وحده باختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes clouds into separate pieces, leaving openings through which rain can descend; al-wadq is abundant, continuous rain emerging through the clouds in either joined or divided states.
rows.anchor: أي قطعا غير متصل بعضها ببعض اتصلا يمنع نزول الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain reaching a land or person God chooses is a sheer favor, not something owed; the recipients owe worship, gratitude, and submission, yet they quickly rejoice in the hoped-for harvest despite possible setbacks.
rows.anchor: ونبه على أن ذلك فضل منه لا يجب عليه لأحد أصلا شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people rejoice at once because they anticipate the beneficial effects of rainfall, such as fertility, moisture, and softness.
rows.anchor: وهو السرور الذي تشرق له البشرة حال الإصابة ظهورا بالغا عظيما بما يرجونه مما يحدث عنه من الأثر النافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns deafness and blindness of the heart, not the physical senses; only someone who continually renews faith is receptive to God's audible and visible signs.
rows.anchor: بينه ببيان أن المراد موت القلب وصممه وعماه لا الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular in the condition shows that redirecting one person is easier than redirecting a group; the plural result signals that many may follow once the method is used.
rows.anchor: وأشار بالإفراد في الشرط إلى أن لفت الواحد عن رأيه أقرب من لفته وهو مع غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who submit are not rigidly bound to imitation but yield fully to evidence; the verse concludes arguments for resurrection through bodily and spiritual signs.
rows.anchor: منقادون للدليل غاية الانقياد غير جامدين مع التقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and ʿAsim, with a difference in the transmission of Hafs, read ḍaʿf with a fatḥa for weakness generally; the other readers use a ḍamma, and the author relates the weakness to the earliest developmental stages.
rows.anchor: وقوى بما أشارت إليه قراءة الباقين بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings move from initial weakness through growth and full strength, then return to weakness and gray hair; the author gives approximate youth and aging milestones and explains gray hair through bodily cooling and dryness.
rows.anchor: من حال الترعرع إلى القوة بالبلوغ إلى التمام في أحد وعشرين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These variable life stages prove God's free choice, knowledge, and power; natural causes cannot thwart what he wills, and his knowledge is named before power because knowledge entails power.
rows.anchor: وقدم صفة العلم لاستتباعها للقدرة التي المقام لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour recreates in less than a blink what unfolded gradually over thousands of years; it is called the Hour because it is easy for God.
rows.anchor: القيامة التي هي إعادة الخلائق الذين كانوا بالتدريج في ألوف من السنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals will swear that they remained in the world and barzakh only a brief hour, speaking from ignorance and their habit of being diverted from truth into doubt and falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي قدر يسير من ليل أو نهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned scream with all their strength and ask God to bring them out so they can do righteous deeds instead of their former work, either admitting error or regretfully recognizing they were wrong.
rows.anchor: أي يوجدون الصراخ فيها بغاية ما يقدرون عليه من الجهد في الصياح بالبكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds them that he gave them sufficient life and reason, delayed their punishment, and allowed any capable person time to mend their affairs; the past tense implies the register of those who remember is closed after resurrection.
rows.anchor: مع إعطائنا لكم العقول ولم نعاجلكم بالأخذ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is cited for sixty years as the period sufficient for reflection; al-Bukhari placed the report in the opening chapters of al-Riqaq.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه ستون سنة - قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that one whom God allows to reach sixty has received sufficient warning regarding lifespan; the author cites Ahmad ibn Maniʿ.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( من عمره الله ستين سنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that the lifespans of his community range from sixty to seventy years, with few exceeding that; the author cites al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Abu Yaʿla.
rows.anchor: وروى الترمذي وابن ماجه وأبو يعلى عن أبي هريرة أيضا رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال (

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers and revealed books supplied warnings that reinforce what reason alone could not establish; after that evidence, the wrongdoers are told to taste their eternal torment, with no helper to rescue them.
rows.anchor: أي عنى من الرسل والكتب تأييدا للعقول بالدليل المعقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-helper statement applies to every wrongdoer: whenever injustice becomes established, it weakens while truth gains strength.
rows.anchor: يعينهم ويقوي أيديهم , فلا براح لكم عن هذا الذواق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of the unseen and of hearts explains the lasting punishment as proportionate to their disbelief; even if their lives were extended or they returned, they would persist in forbidden acts.
rows.anchor: فهو يعلم أنكم لو مدت أعماركم لم ترجعوا عن الكفر أبدا , ولو رددتم لعدتم لما نهيتم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may know a person's final fate before any thought exists: someone apparently righteous can die wretched, while a deeply corrupt person may turn sincerely toward good and die among the blessed; angels and devils may learn later thoughts once they arise.
rows.anchor: يأمر الملك أن يكتب عند نفخ الروح في الولد أنه ما شقي أو سعيد قبل أن يكون له خاطر أصلا
